newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2914 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2925 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to active buying after the main 8.2920 resistance level was breached, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2925.
Dealers said buying became active when the yuan broke through the 8.2920 level at the mid-session with the People's Bank, the central bank, taking no action to depress the yuan.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2915 and fell to hit an intraday low of 8.2923 early in trading. It then rose and stood firmly above 8.2920 after the mid-session, hitting a high of 8.2911.
Trading was active early in the session but dull in late trading with most business done at 8.2915, traders said.
One dealer said the central bank did not intervene when the yuan breached the 8.2920 resistance level, encouraging more buying which made the yuan close much higher.
A second dealer said after Thursday's close, the yuan had entered a range where the central bank usually intervened to prevent the local currency from rising sharply.
"Caution might lead the yuan to end slightly down on Friday," he said.
The yuan closed higher but at an intraday low of 7.3100 from 7.3250 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0715 from 1.0724 against the Hong Kong dollar.
